Scope: Read-only review requested by root after the actual A-to-B-to-A Liuli regression fix
Status: No reachable command/checkpoint scalar injection found
Observations: The return owns its scalar cutoff and frozen finalized cursor; initial cutoff is zero, and the only later native write sets the old candidate count immediately after actual RedirectCurrentAttack issuance before appending the new target episode.
Target owner bindings are admitted only when candidateIndex is at or after the cutoff and the active native attack target matches their owner; non-target bindings keep their existing scope.

The exact-return predicate checks the cutoff range, not a separately issued cutoff ledger. Arbitrary trusted frame replacement could construct another in-range cutoff, but command and checkpoint input do not deserialize or replace runtime frames.

GameCheckpoint stores immutable setup and accepted commands. GameReplay.Restore calls command Replay and checks revision, mode, package signatures, content hash and rules compatibility. Public ResolutionStack is trusted diagnostics returned as a read-only list; the scalar and frame fields are init-only records.
AnswerPromptCommand accepts actor, prompt id, choice id and revision; it carries no runtime cursor or mutable PromptChoice parameters. The accepted choice comes from the published exact prompt.

No command or checkpoint restore path was found that supplies an arbitrary in-range cutoff. This is static input-boundary analysis, not a proof against arbitrary host reflection or future direct-frame restoration APIs.
Limits: No private-frame reflection or arbitrary host-memory replacement was treated as a player input path.
The helper predicate alone is not claimed to authenticate the scalar against an independent cutoff issuance event.
